newsitem.title: GERMANY: German spring barley crop to rise 40 pct - broker.
newsitem.headline: German spring barley crop to rise 40 pct - broker.

text.p: Germany's 1996 spring barley crop may rise by a staggering 40 percent to four million tonnes this year due to area increases and beneficial weather, specialist malting barley broker Jochen Mautner said.
"Some 60 percent of the crop may qualify for malting purposes, provided that remaining areas bring similarly good qualities as those harvested to date," Mautner said.
Rain was hampering the harvest, which was already delayed by two weeks after a harsh winter. If it continued, it could cause premature sprouting, which spoils barley for malting.
But some 70 percent of the crop had already been cut.
Mautner said precipitation and temperatures since May had been ideal for yields, offsetting late sowings and a cold and dry start to the summer.
Total spring barley sowings had increased by 20 percent over 1995 to 793,000 hectares, as damaged winter barley and rapeseed areas were replanted, especially in eastern Germany.
But barley on resown areas usually developed less favourable malting qualities than that on other land.
Protein contents were an average 10.7 percent, similar to last year's low 10.8 percent, which is desirable for malting.

Prices had eased under harvest pressure and European prices were also falling because Germany now looked set to import sharply lower volumes this year. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
